title: Multiple failed SSH logins followed by success
details: 187 failed SSH logins for the root account from EXTERNAL-HOST-01 in four minutes, followed by one successful root login from that host.
explanation: A burst of failures followed by a success from one external address is consistent with a successful brute-force attack. Treat the root account as potentially compromised.

title: Account locked after repeated failed logins
details: A standard user account locked after five failed logins at 08:02 from WORKSTATION-01. The same account successfully signed in from that workstation at 08:04 on a Monday morning.
explanation: The same account and workstation, followed by a successful login two minutes later, are consistent with a mistyped password rather than an attack.

title: User submitted credentials to a suspicious sign-in page
details: An email from MAIL-SENDER-01 asked a user to verify a mailbox. Proxy telemetry shows a credential submission to a lookalike sign-in domain registered two days earlier.
explanation: A lookalike sender, urgency, and credential submission to a newly registered domain indicate credential phishing. Reset the password and revoke active sessions.

title: Port scan detected inside the network
details: APPROVED-SCANNER-01 probed 1,000 ports across SCAN-SUBNET-01 in 60 seconds. The asset is a registered vulnerability scanner and the activity matches approved change CHG-EXAMPLE-01.
explanation: An approved scanner running inside its scheduled change window is expected. Confirming the asset and approved change is what clears this alert.

title: Port scan from a user workstation
details: USER-WORKSTATION-01 probed 15 ports each on a domain controller and file server at 22:10. No change is recorded and no scanning tool is approved on this host.
explanation: A standard user workstation has no expected reason to scan servers. This may indicate reconnaissance by malware or an intruder; isolate and investigate the host.

title: Suspicious PowerShell launched from Word
details: WINWORD.EXE on WORKSTATION-02 spawned powershell.exe with an encoded command, which then connected to EXTERNAL-HOST-02 on port 443.
explanation: Word should not normally launch encoded PowerShell. The unusual child process and outbound callback warrant investigation as a possible malicious document.

title: PowerShell executed as SYSTEM
details: PowerShell ran Get-WindowsUpdateLog at 02:00 as SYSTEM under the established WeeklyMaintenance task, created by IT six months ago and scheduled for Sundays.
explanation: A longstanding scheduled task running a built-in maintenance command on its normal schedule is routine administration.

title: Unusual sign-in with repeated MFA prompts
details: USER-01 signed in from Nairobi at 09:12, then from a distant location at 09:41 on a new device. The second sign-in followed six denied MFA prompts and one approval.
explanation: A geographically implausible sign-in, a new device, and repeated denied prompts ending in approval are consistent with MFA fatigue. Verify with the user and revoke suspicious sessions.

title: Impossible travel detected
details: USER-02 signed in from Nairobi at 14:05 and a Netherlands VPN exit node at 14:25. The device identifier is unchanged and there were no failed attempts; the VPN provider is approved.
explanation: The approved VPN exit point, unchanged device, and absence of failed attempts explain the location jump as VPN routing.

title: SQL injection attempt on a web application
details: Requests to a product endpoint contained common SQL injection test strings and originated from WEB-CLIENT-01. The last response was HTTP 200 and ten times larger than normal.
explanation: Injection-like requests followed by an unusually large successful response may indicate data was returned. Review application logs and response behavior, and remediate any confirmed weakness.

title: WAF blocked possible SQL injection
details: A POST from the authenticated staff editor was blocked. The request body contains the ordinary sentence SELECT the best option from the list inside an article draft.
explanation: The word SELECT appears in ordinary prose from an authenticated editor. The context suggests a keyword rule over-match rather than an injection attempt.

title: High-volume DNS TXT queries
details: DNS-SOURCE-01 made 4,200 DNS TXT queries in one hour to random subdomains of a reserved example domain. The average query length was 180 characters.
explanation: Long random subdomains and high-volume TXT lookups can indicate data being moved through DNS. Investigate the source host and destination domain.

title: DNS spike to a single domain
details: Forty hosts queried the approved example antivirus update domain between 06:00 and 06:05, as they do each day.
explanation: Many hosts contacting a known vendor domain at the same time each day is consistent with scheduled antivirus updates.

title: Large upload to personal cloud storage
details: A generic user account uploaded a 4.2 GB archive to a personal cloud storage site at 23:47. The account's usual uploads are under 50 MB, and an HR departure notice is recorded.
explanation: Unusual volume, after-hours timing, a personal storage destination, and a recorded departure may indicate data theft. Preserve evidence and follow the organization's response process.

title: Large outbound data transfer
details: BACKUP-SERVER-01 sent 600 GB to the approved backup vault at 01:00. This matches the nightly backup job and is within five percent of each of the last 30 nights.
explanation: The same source, destination, schedule, and consistent size indicate a normal offsite backup rather than data exfiltration.

title: Mass file modification
details: On FILE-SERVER-01, 3,200 files were renamed with a .locked extension in 90 seconds. A recovery note appeared in each folder, and a command to delete shadow copies was executed.
explanation: Rapid mass renaming, a ransom note, and deletion of shadow copies are strong ransomware indicators. Isolate the server and follow incident response procedures.

title: New account added to Domain Admins
details: A generic service account was created and added to Domain Admins at 03:14 by ADMIN-01. No change is recorded. ADMIN-01 normally works business hours and is marked away.
explanation: An unapproved privileged account created at night by an account marked away may indicate credential compromise or persistence. Verify with the account owner and investigate.

title: New account added to Domain Admins
details: A generic service account was created and added to Domain Admins at 10:30 by the IT manager. It matches approved onboarding request HR-EXAMPLE-01.
explanation: The account, timing, actor, and approved onboarding request line up. Context distinguishes this expected change from an otherwise similar serious alert.

title: Remote Desktop login to database server
details: DBA-USER-01 logged in via RDP to DB-SERVER-01 at 14:20 from approved JUMP-HOST-01. MFA succeeded and the login occurred during business hours.
explanation: Administrative access through the approved jump host with MFA during working hours is the intended secure path.

title: Malware detected by antivirus
details: Antivirus detected the harmless EICAR test string on TEST-HOST-01 during a security awareness exercise. The file was quarantined immediately.
explanation: EICAR is a harmless standard test string designed to trigger antivirus detection. The alert confirms that the control is working.
